props.text: Enhance your look with minimal downtime.
A surgeon's training. An artist's eye.
She reads the whole face, not the one feature you came in about.

Dr. Stone came to surgery through engineering: a biomedical engineering degree, then a Doctorate of Dental Surgery, then a full oral and maxillofacial residency across three Level 1 trauma centres. That path is why she plans in three dimensions and thinks in structure before she thinks in skin.
It also means the plan you leave with is hers. She is the one who assesses you, the one who operates, and the one you see afterwards. No handoffs, no rotating providers.
Most surgeons replace what's missing. I design what belongs.
Three steps, and no surprises in any of them.
An hour with Dr. Stone, not with a coordinator. You leave knowing what is possible, what is not, and what each option costs.
A written plan with the technique, the recovery and the fee set out. Financing through Sunbit if you want to spread it.
Your procedure, then follow-up with the same surgeon, through the swelling, the settling and the year it takes to look like you always did.
Patients talk about the same two things.
Being listened to, and not being sold to. Both come up more often than any procedure does.

I went in looking for lip fillers wanting the “sexy pout”. Dr. Stone talked me through the process and told me she would not overfill for the sake of having big lips. Which I loved. She said we would start small and work our way up. I am in love with my lips. Plump but natural.

Dr. Stone will hear your concerns and give you all of your options. At no point will you feel pressured in your treatment choices. I started out with more of a conservative maintenance with my cosmetic facial routine and I couldn't be happier with the results.
Dr. Stone and her staff made me feel comfortable and welcomed. My eyelid surgery went very well and I am very pleased. I highly recommend her!
Dr. Stone is so kind and also a great, proactive surgeon. Not only do I send patients to her, I am one myself. The office and staff are equally fantastic.

Absolutely beautiful office with cutting-edge equipment. The staff at Stone Surgical Arts are an amazing team. Dr. Stone is an incredible surgeon, she takes the time to talk through procedures and treatment plans with her patients.

Four months ago I took my daughter to Dr. Stone with her face covered with acne, and through the past few months she has helped my daughter clear her skin tremendously. It's a friendly environment and she's the sweetest doctor ever.
The work speaks in pairs of photographs.
Neck lifts, blepharoplasty, chin and jawline work, fillers and resurfacing, filtered by treatment so you can look only at the one you came for, alongside what patients say afterwards.

The gallery and its before-and-after comparison are built and working. Cases are published only with the patient's current written consent, so it fills as the practice's own photography is shot and cleared.
Credit that banks instead of expiring.

Aesthetic care is rarely one appointment. A membership turns a monthly amount into credit that accumulates until you want it: a syringe this spring, or a surgical fee next year, with member pricing on everything in between.
Where Dr. Stone has been asked to speak.

The five questions we are asked most.
What does the consultation cost, and what happens in it?

$175 for Texas residents and $250 from out of state, with a $100 deposit to hold the appointment that comes off the fee. You spend the hour with Dr. Stone rather than a treatment coordinator, and you leave with the options, the honest limits of each, and what each one costs.
How much time will I need away from work?

The practice's own guidance: about a week after eyelid surgery, about ten days after CO2 laser resurfacing, and two weeks after a facelift. Plan for one to two weeks of private time and come back early if recovery goes better than expected. It is always easier that way round than the reverse.

Will I need someone to drive me home?

For anything under intravenous sedation, yes. A responsible adult has to bring you, stay in the office through the procedure and drive you home, and you should not drive or operate machinery for 24 hours afterwards. Treatments done under local anaesthetic alone do not require it.
When can I wear makeup again?
In most cases 48 hours after sutures come out. After CO2 laser, about ten days. Sun avoidance matters more than makeup does in that window: sun on healing skin is what darkens a scar.

pages.seoDescription: Every treatment Stone Surgical Arts offers, in four categories, with published fees. Face, neck and jawline, skin, and non-surgical, in Westlake, Texas.

props.text: Everything the practice offers, in one place, with the fee beside it. If a treatment is not right for you, Dr. Stone will say so at the consultation rather than after it.
An hour with the surgeon who would perform your procedure. A $100 deposit holds the appointment and comes off the consultation fee.
Read this first if you are not sure which column you belong in. The fee schedule underneath repeats every treatment named here, with its price beside it.

Facial surgery here starts at the bone and works outward. Implants are planned in three dimensions and made for your anatomy rather than picked from a tray of stock sizes. The practice’s own position is that a generic implant gives a generic result. Eyelid surgery tightens and smooths the upper or lower lid where drooping and puffiness make a rested face look tired. Buccal fat reduction slims a heavy mid-face, and is planned conservatively because it does not grow back.
Most face procedures are outpatient. Plan about a week away after eyelid surgery, and two weeks after a facelift.
The part of ageing that shows first.

A neck lift, a lower rhytidectomy, combines liposuction, skin removal and muscle tightening in whatever proportion your anatomy needs, and the practice puts the result at five to ten years. MyEllevate® is the lighter option: an outpatient procedure under local anaesthetic, guided by an ICLED® light, that suspends the muscle with a suture instead of opening the neck. It suits earlier laxity, where a neck lift reverses the more advanced kind. Which one you are is the question the consultation answers.
This is the work that earned Dr. Stone the name “Dr. Jawline”. Jaw and chin surgery is the practice’s most requested.
Resurfacing, and the regenerative work underneath it.

Fractionated CO2 drives short microbeams of heat into the deeper skin layers so collagen rebuilds. The practice quotes about ten days of downtime and puts it to work on fine lines, dark spots, acne scarring, enlarged pores and sun damage. Morpheus8 does related work sub-dermally, usually across one to three sessions. Chemical peels lift the top layers so newer skin comes up, and are the first answer to hyperpigmentation. PRP and PRF sit behind all of it, using your own platelets so the healing does more of the work.
Microneedling is sold in packages of three. Quoted fees are face-only, and additional areas cost extra.
The maintenance that keeps surgery further away.

Neuromodulators soften the lines expression carves in, and are priced per unit rather than per area, so you pay for what you actually need. Fillers raise and fill without an incision, general anaesthetic or recovery: lips, folds, acne scarring, the hollows that come with volume loss. Sculptra works more slowly and more structurally, in a course rather than a session. Hair restoration and fat transfer round it out.
Injectables are with Brooke, a board-certified nurse practitioner and advanced aesthetic injector. Botox starts working two to three days after injection and is at its full effect around day ten.

, an application that takes about a minute and does not affect your credit score to check. For ongoing treatment rather than a one-off procedure, a membership is usually the cheaper route: the monthly amount becomes credit that accumulates instead of expiring.
The comparisons people get stuck on.
If your question is here, the answer is the practice’s own. If it is not, it is a consultation question, and that is not a deflection, it is that the honest answer depends on your anatomy.
MyEllevate® or a neck lift: how do I know which?

A neck lift uses small incisions behind the ears and under the chin to reach the tissue underneath, and delivers a result that can last up to ten years. MyEllevate® places internal sutures through small punctures instead, and lasts around five. MyEllevate® suits earlier laxity; a neck lift reverses more advanced sagging, wrinkling or fullness. It is also a practical difference on the day: MyEllevate® needs only local anaesthetic, so you can drive yourself home.
Will a neck lift fix my jowls?

No, and this is the most common mix-up. Jowls sit low on the face, so people assume they are neck work, but they originate in sagging facial tissue and are addressed in a facelift, not a neck lift. A minimally invasive facelift is the procedure that reduces them.

Fillers are gel injectables that plump and smooth lines, acne scars and thin lips, and last from months to a couple of years depending on the product and the site. Implants are customised inserts that reshape the underlying structure and are made from a biocompatible material that stays intact, so the contour is permanent. Filler changes the surface; an implant changes the frame.
How long does each result actually last?

The practice’s own published figures: blepharoplasty 10–15 years or more; a neck lift up to ten; MyEllevate® around five; facial implants and buccal fat reduction permanent, though significant weight gain can put fullness back into the cheek elsewhere. Injectables are months, not years, which is what makes them maintenance rather than surgery.
Can I have more than one procedure at once?

Often, and it is frequently the better plan: a neck lift can be done alongside a facelift or eyelid surgery in a single procedure, with one recovery instead of two. What can be combined safely depends on your anatomy and how long you would be under anaesthetic, so it is decided at the consultation rather than in advance.
Why do some rows say “at consultation” instead of a price?

Because the practice never published a figure for those, and we would rather show you a gap than a guess. Genioplasty, fat transfer and facelift fees genuinely vary with the case, as the practice’s own pages say. Everything else on this page carries the fee the practice published, which is being reconfirmed for 2026.

She came to surgery through engineering, and it shows in the planning.
Before dental school, Dr. Stone took a degree in
. Then a Doctorate of Dental Surgery from the University of Missouri–Kansas City, then a full residency in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery in Fort Lauderdale, across
, where the work is rebuilding faces that have been broken.
She is an attending surgeon at

, sits on Pinnacle faculty, and is certified in KLS Martin IPS® patient-specific implant planning: the workflow where an implant is designed to a particular skull from a particular scan, rather than fitted from a tray of stock sizes.

What that background produces is a surgeon who reads proportion the way a plastic surgeon does: the line of the jaw, the balance across the mid-face, how a feature will sit in ten years. She plans in three dimensions before touching anything.
Most surgeons replace what's missing. I design what belongs.

A degree in biomedical engineering, which is why she plans in three dimensions and thinks about load and structure before she thinks about skin.

Maxillofacial pathology, dentoalveolar and implant surgery, maxillofacial reconstruction, microvascular surgery, trauma, and facial cosmetic surgery. Attending surgeon at Baylor Medical Center in Grapevine and Irving, and at Methodist.

Plan for longer than you need, and come back early.

The practice’s own guidance, and it is worth reading before you book rather than after. Give yourself one to two weeks of private time. That does not mean housebound; it means not scheduling anything you would be sorry to attend swollen.

About a week after eyelid surgery. About ten days after CO2 laser resurfacing. Two weeks after a facelift. Always plan for more time and return early if it is going well. That is easier than the reverse.

Walk immediately. Nothing that raises a sweat for two weeks, and nothing over 10 lb. From day 15, up to 20 lb plus non-impact cardio. From day 21, jogging and swimming. After a facelift, no lifting or sharp head turns for six weeks.

Makeup over incisions 48 hours after sutures come out; about ten days after CO2. Sun avoidance matters more: sun on healing skin is what darkens a scar. Broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher from two weeks, until the pink has gone.

In the first two to four weeks a general melancholy is common, and many patients quietly question the decision. It is normal, and it lifts as you feel physically better. Do not expect family and friends to comment, because people are busy. You had this done for your own reasons, and yours is the opinion that counts.

pages.seoTitle: Face & Neck Lift Westlake TX | Stone Surgical Arts
pages.seoDescription: The full procedure, face and neck addressed together, because the two age as one structure and lifting only half of it shows.

props.text: The full procedure, face and neck addressed together, because the two age as one structure and lifting only half of it shows.

A face lift is not about pulling skin tight. Skin is the last layer, and treating it as the problem is how a face ends up looking operated on rather than rested. The work happens underneath, in the layer of muscle and fascia that has descended, and the skin is redraped over the result rather than dragged into position.

Face and neck are quoted and performed together here. Lifting the face and leaving the neck produces a mismatch that most patients notice within a year, and the neck is the harder half of the operation, which is the half this practice is known for.

This is the right operation when there is genuine descent and genuine skin excess, rather than early laxity that a suture suspension could still hold. It tends to be patients in their fifties and sixties, and younger patients who have lost a large amount of weight.
Jowling along the jaw, where the jawline has lost its edge
Deep folds running from the nose to the corners of the mouth
Loose skin in the neck that does not retract when you lift your chin
A previous lift that has relaxed and needs revising
If your skin still has good tone and the problem is muscle rather than excess, Dr. Stone will tell you that and point you at
instead. Being talked out of the bigger operation is a normal outcome of a consultation here.
The lift restores position. It does not change the quality of the skin on top of it, or reopen an eye that has hooded, so two things are commonly planned alongside it:
, because a lifted face with tired eyes reads as tired.
, for the texture and pigment a lift cannot reach. Often staged rather than done the same day.
Both are decided at the consultation, on your anatomy, and neither is sold as a package beforehand.

The facial nerve branches run through the plane this operation works in. Knowing where they are on a diagram is not the same as knowing where they are in a particular face, at a particular depth, under tension. Dr. Stone trained in oral and maxillofacial surgery across three Level 1 trauma centres, rebuilding this anatomy after it had been broken, which is the least forgiving way to learn it.
She plans and performs every case herself. The surgeon who assesses you is the surgeon who operates on you and the surgeon you see at every follow-up.
Recovery figures are typical, not a promise. Yours is set out in your written plan.
What the day actually looks like.

Four to six hours under general anaesthetic, depending on what is being combined. You are monitored afterwards and go home the same day with a responsible adult, or stay overnight if that is the safer plan for you.

Swelling and bruising peak around day three and fall away quickly after that. Sutures come out in stages across the first two weeks. Most people are presentable to people who are not looking for it at around two weeks.
The result keeps refining for six to twelve months as swelling resolves and scars mature. Follow-ups are with Dr. Stone, not with a nurse you have not met.
What people ask before they book.
Where do the scars go, and will people see them?

They follow the natural creases in front of the ear, around the earlobe and back into the hairline behind it. They are placed where the anatomy hides them and they mature over months from pink to pale. Scar care starts as soon as the wounds are closed and is part of your plan, not an afterthought.

A well-executed lift resets the clock rather than stopping it. Most patients look substantially better than their unoperated baseline for a decade or more, and you continue to age normally from the new starting point. Skin quality, weight stability, sun exposure and genetics all move that figure, and Dr. Stone will give you a realistic number for your face rather than an average.
Will I look like a different person?

No, and if a result looks like a different person then something has gone wrong with the planning. The aim is that people register that you look well rather than that you look altered. That is a matter of how much tension is placed on which layer, and it is decided in the operating theatre rather than promised beforehand.

props.text: The upper third of the face, opened back up. Often the reason a face reads as tired when nothing else about it has changed.

The forehead and brows descend before almost anything else, and they do it slowly enough that most people never identify them as the problem. What they notice is that they look cross, or tired, or that eye makeup has stopped sitting where it used to.
A brow lift repositions the brow and releases the muscles that pull it down. It is a smaller operation than most people expect and it changes expression more than any other procedure on this list.

The test is simple and you can do it in front of a mirror: lift the skin at the tail of the brow with a fingertip. If that single millimetre opens the eye and softens the expression, this is your operation rather than an eyelid one.
Brows that sit low or have flattened out at the tail
A heavy, hooded look through the upper lid that lifting the brow relieves
Deep horizontal lines that no longer soften when the face is at rest
A permanently stern or tired expression that does not match your mood

The order matters. The brow is lifted first, then the lid is assessed against its new position, because doing it the other way round removes skin the brow was going to give back.

There is a height at which a brow looks alert and a height at which it looks startled, and the distance between the two is a few millimetres. It is also different for every face, and different between men and women, where a flatter, lower brow is usually the goal rather than an arched one.
This is why the planning is drawn on your own measurements rather than applied from a template. A brow lift that is technically clean and two millimetres too high is a bad result.
Recovery figures are typical, not a promise. Yours is set out in your written plan.
What the day actually looks like.
One to two hours. Sedation is enough for most cases; general anaesthetic where it is combined with a larger procedure. You go home the same day with someone to drive you.
Swelling settles downward into the eyelids for the first few days, which is expected and passes. Numbness across the scalp is normal early on. Most people are back at a desk at around ten days.
The brow drops slightly from its immediate post-operative position over the first weeks, which is planned for. The final height is what you see at three to six months.
What people ask before they book.

That is the classic bad brow lift and it comes from over-elevating the medial brow, the end nearest the nose. The modern approach lifts the tail rather than the middle and releases the muscles that depress the brow, which opens the eye without raising the whole forehead. It is a planning decision, made against your measurements, before anything is touched.

That depends on the technique chosen for your anatomy and hairline, and it is settled at the consultation rather than assumed here. In every version they sit within or behind the hairline where the anatomy conceals them.
Could I just use Botox instead?

For a small amount of tail elevation, sometimes yes, and it is a reasonable place to start if you are not ready for surgery. A neuromodulator relaxes the muscles pulling the brow down and can buy a millimetre or two. It cannot reposition a brow that has genuinely descended, and it needs repeating three or four times a year.
Will it help my hooded eyelids?

Often substantially, because a good deal of what people call hooding is brow sitting on lid. Whether you also need eyelid skin removed is judged with the brow held in its intended new position, not with it where it is today.

props.text: Eyelid surgery, upper or lower. The smallest operation on this list and, for most faces, the one that changes the most.

People look at eyes. It is the first thing a face is read by, and it is where fatigue registers whether or not you are tired. Eyelid surgery removes or repositions the tissue that has made the eye look smaller and heavier than it is.
It is a short operation with a quick recovery and a very high satisfaction rate, which is why it is often the first procedure someone has and frequently the only one they need.
Upper and lower lids are different problems and they are assessed separately, though both are commonly done in one sitting.

The part that is easy to get wrong

Lower lids punish over-resection. Take too much skin or too much fat and the lid pulls away from the eye, which is difficult to correct and immediately obvious. Modern technique is therefore conservative and increasingly about repositioning fat into the hollow beneath rather than removing it.

Dr. Stone trained in oral and maxillofacial surgery across three Level 1 trauma centres, which is where the orbit and the tissues around it are reconstructed after injury. It is a demanding way to learn an anatomy that leaves very little room for error.

One to two hours under local anaesthetic with sedation, depending on whether both upper and lower lids are being done. You go home the same day with someone to drive you.
Bruising is the main event and it is worst around days two and three. Cold compresses and sleeping propped up shorten it considerably. Fine sutures come out at around a week.
Most people are comfortable in company at ten days and in photographs at three weeks. The last of the swelling in the lid resolves over two to three months.

On the upper lid the incision sits in the natural crease and disappears into it once healed. On the lower lid it is placed just beneath the lash line, or inside the lid entirely where only fat is being addressed, in which case there is no external scar at all.
Upper eyelid surgery is generally a once in a lifetime operation for most patients. Lower lids are similarly durable. You continue to age, but the tissue that was removed does not come back.

They address different things. Filler can soften a hollow under the eye and laser can improve the texture of thin lid skin, and for early changes either may be enough. Neither removes excess skin or repositions herniated fat, which is what makes a lid look heavy.

props.text: Structure, restored where the bone never provided it or where time has taken it. Planned to the skeleton, placed through the mouth, and reversible.

Some faces have not lost volume. They were built with less projection through the cheekbone or the chin, and no amount of filler placed in the soft tissue above will substitute for the platform that is missing underneath.

An implant addresses the skeleton directly. It is a permanent, precisely shaped augmentation that sits on the bone, and because it is a solid object in a fixed position it does not migrate, dissolve or need topping up.
The clearest candidates are people who have been offered filler repeatedly and have never been satisfied with it, because the deficiency they are trying to correct is structural.
A flat or hollow midface where the cheekbone gives no definition in profile
A chin that sits back from the rest of the face, which makes the nose read as larger and the neck as shorter
Facial balance that photographs poorly in profile despite everything looking reasonable head on
Volume loss that filler improves for a few months at a time and never actually solves

A recessed chin is worth singling out. It is one of the most under-diagnosed features in facial aesthetics, and correcting it changes the apparent size of the nose and the definition of the jawline without touching either.
Implants set the frame. What sits on top of it is frequently addressed in the same plan:

Planned to your bone, and reversible

Implants are sized and shaped against your own skeletal measurements rather than selected from a small range of stock sizes and hoped for. That planning is the difference between an implant that reads as your own bone and one that reads as an implant.
They are also removable. That is a genuine and underrated advantage over anything permanent that cannot be undone: if it is ever not right, it comes out, and the anatomy returns to where it started.
Dr. Stone trained in oral and maxillofacial surgery across three Level 1 trauma centres. Placing hardware on facial bone through the mouth is the core of that specialty rather than an addition to it.
Recovery figures are typical, not a promise. Yours is set out in your written plan.
What the day actually looks like.

One to two hours, under sedation or general anaesthetic depending on what is combined. Access is through the mouth for both cheek and chin in most cases, so there is no external incision. Same day home.

Swelling is the main feature and it is significant for the first week. A soft diet and careful oral hygiene for that period. Numbness of the lower lip after a chin implant is common early on and resolves.
The shape you will keep emerges as swelling resolves over six to eight weeks. The implant itself does not change after that.
What people ask before they book.
Can it be removed if I change my mind?

Yes, and that is one of the strongest arguments for an implant over the alternatives. It is a discrete object in a defined pocket. Removal is a smaller procedure than placement and the anatomy returns to its starting point.

Filler sits in soft tissue and behaves like soft tissue. On a face that lacks skeletal projection it adds width and fullness rather than definition, which is why repeated syringes so often fail to produce the profile the patient wanted. An implant replaces missing structure with structure.
Will there be a scar on my face?

In most cases no. Cheek and chin implants are usually placed through an incision inside the mouth, which leaves nothing visible externally. Where an external approach under the chin is the better choice for a particular anatomy, that is discussed and agreed beforehand.
Do implants wear out or need replacing?

No. They are inert, they do not dissolve, and they do not have a service life. They are replaced only if you want a different result or, rarely, if there is a problem such as infection, which is uncommon and is discussed as part of consent.

The buccal fat pad is a defined structure sitting in the hollow of the cheek, separate from the fat immediately under the skin. In some faces it is large enough to blunt the line between cheekbone and jaw, producing fullness that has nothing to do with weight and does not respond to losing any.
Reducing it is a short procedure through a small incision inside the mouth. There is no external scar and the recovery is measured in days.

Faces lose volume with age, and removing structural fat from a face that will thin anyway produces a gaunt, hollowed look a decade later that is very difficult to reverse.

This procedure is popular for reasons that have more to do with photography than with anatomy, and it is permanent. Fat that is removed does not return, and a face that reads as sculpted at thirty can read as drawn at forty-five.

props.text: Shortens the space between nose and lip and rolls the upper lip outward. A permanent alternative to filler, and a different result from it.

The distance between the base of the nose and the top of the lip lengthens over a lifetime. As it does, the upper lip rolls inward and less of it shows, the teeth stop showing at rest, and the mouth reads as older regardless of how much volume is in the lip itself.

A lip lift removes a small, precisely measured strip of skin beneath the nose. The lip moves up, rolls outward, and shows more of itself. It changes proportion, which is something no amount of filler can do.
The measurement that matters is the philtral height, and there is a range that reads as youthful for a given face. Beyond it, the mouth looks long whatever else is done.
A long space between the base of the nose and the lip
An upper lip that has thinned and rolled inward with age
No upper tooth showing when the mouth is at rest
Repeated filler that has produced volume without ever producing shape

That last one is the most common story. Filler adds bulk to a lip that is rolled inward, which pushes it forward rather than revealing it, and the result is a lip that is larger but no more visible. If that is your history, this is probably the operation you actually wanted.

It does not add volume. A lip lift reveals lip that already exists by changing its position; it does not make a thin lip full. Where both shape and volume are wanted, a modest amount of filler after the lift has healed does the second job, and much less of it is needed once the proportion is right.

It also leaves a scar. The incision sits in the crease at the base of the nose where the anatomy hides it, and it matures to be difficult to find, but it is a permanent scar on the face and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling something.

The amount of skin removed is measured in single millimetres and there is no margin for approximation. Too little and nothing has changed; too much and the mouth cannot close comfortably and the result is unmistakably surgical.
The marking is done against your own measurements, at rest and in animation, and it is checked before anything is cut. This is a small operation in which the planning is most of the work.
Recovery figures are typical, not a promise. Yours is set out in your written plan.
What the day actually looks like.
About an hour under local anaesthetic, with sedation if you would prefer it. The marking is checked, the strip of skin removed and the wound closed in layers with very fine sutures.
Swelling of the upper lip is pronounced for several days and looks like far too much has been done. It is not. Sutures come out at around five to seven days.

Pink and visible for the first couple of months, then fading steadily. Scar care starts as soon as the sutures are out and continues for months, because that is what determines how well it disappears.
What people ask before they book.
How visible is the scar, honestly?

It sits in the crease where the nose meets the lip, which is one of the best hiding places on the face. In most patients it matures to a fine pale line that is hard to see at conversational distance. It is permanent, it is on your face, and how it heals depends on your skin, your genetics and how diligently you do the scar care.
Is it better than lip filler?

It is different, not better. Filler adds volume and is reversible and temporary. A lip lift changes proportion and is permanent. If your complaint is that your lips are thin, filler is the answer. If your complaint is that your mouth looks long and your upper lip has disappeared, filler will not fix it and this will.
Can I still have filler afterwards?
Yes, once healed, and most patients need considerably less of it than they were having before. The lift makes the lip visible; filler then adjusts volume within a shape that is already right.
It should show slightly more upper tooth at rest, which is the point. Your smile itself is produced by muscle that is not disturbed, so the animation stays yours.

Surgery repositions. Injectables fill and relax. Neither does anything about the actual quality of the skin: the fine crepe, the sun damage, the pigment, the texture that makes a face look weathered even when its structure is good.

Resurfacing removes a controlled depth of damaged skin and lets it heal from below with new collagen. It is the treatment that makes a good surgical result look genuinely refreshed rather than merely lifted.

Lighter resurfacing is usually a course of two or three spaced weeks apart. A deeper CO2 treatment is frequently a single event with results that last years. Which route suits you is decided against your skin and your calendar.
Is it safe for darker skin?

It requires more care. Darker skin types carry a real risk of post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, which is manageable with the right settings, appropriate pre-treatment and disciplined aftercare, but it changes the plan. This is assessed honestly before anything is booked rather than discovered afterwards.

Usually it is staged rather than combined, because both the skin and the surgical result need to heal without competing. The sequence is planned as part of your overall timeline.

props.text: Neuromodulators and filler, placed by the practice nurse injector, with Dr. Stone available for anything structural.

Injectables do two entirely different jobs that get spoken about as one. Neuromodulators relax the muscles that fold the skin. Fillers replace volume that has been lost or was never there. Confusing the two is how people end up with a face that is smooth and heavy at the same time.
Both are placed here by Brooke, the practice nurse injector. Anything structural, or any case that needs a surgical eye, is seen by Dr. Stone.

Botox, Jeuveau and Dysport all relax muscle. They are dosed and priced per unit, and the units are not interchangeable between brands, which is why comparing the unit price between them is meaningless.

They work on lines produced by movement. A line that is present when your face is completely still is an etched line, and it needs resurfacing or filler rather than a neuromodulator.
Filler replaces volume. Where it is placed matters far more than how much of it is used, and the common failure of this treatment is chasing a hollow with more product until the face is heavy.

Why is Dysport cheaper per unit?

Because a Dysport unit is not equivalent to a Botox unit and the dosing is different. Comparing per unit prices between brands tells you nothing useful. Ask what the treatment costs for your face, which is the number that matters.
Can filler be dissolved if I do not like it?

Hyaluronic acid fillers can be dissolved with an enzyme, which is one of their genuine advantages. Sculptra cannot: it stimulates your own collagen over months and is not reversible, which is why it is dosed conservatively across sessions.
How often will I need it repeated?

Neuromodulators every three to four months. Hyaluronic acid filler generally lasts six to eighteen months depending on the product and the area. Sculptra is built over a course and then maintained annually.
